samples.summary: Paste path bypasses the new fontSize / image-size bands, so a pasted value enters the model out of band and every *other* reader re-reads it banded (divergent render; image silently dropped)
samples.evidence: The diff installs `normalizeFontSize` / `isPaintableImageSize` at the two CRDT read boundaries (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:77-105`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:195-217`), but the clipboard sanitizer — the other producer that writes these fields into the model and on into the CRDT — still admits any finite number: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:141-145` (`const numericKeys = ['letterSpacing','fontSize']` → `asNumber`, which is finite-only, clipboard.ts:69-71) and `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:113-116` (`asNumber(value.width)` / `asNumber(value.height)` for an inline image). Unlike `rowHeights`, which the diff *also* clamps at the one layout sink (`view/table-layout.ts:253`), nothing clamps a pasted `fontSize` or image size on the way to layout. Result: the pasting client holds `fontSize: 1e9` / a 1e9-px image while every peer, the same user after reload, revision preview, the PDF painter and the markdown export read it through the new bands — the font clamps to 400 and the image inline is dropped entirely by `isPaintableImageSize`. The fix belongs on the paste sanitizer (reuse `normalizeFontSize` / `isPaintableImageSize` there), not on the new module.

samples.summary: DOCX import can produce values outside the new bands: a legal Word font size >400pt silently clamps for every reader, and a large declared picture extent makes the image vanish on the next read
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:50` sets `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` with no ceiling (Word's own UI allows up to 1638 pt), and `packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:215-216` computes image `width`/`height` from EMU (`emusToPx(ref.cx)`) with no ceiling. Neither passes through the new bands, but everything that later *reads* the ingested document does: `normalizeFontSize` clamps to `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 400` (`packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:47-51`) and `isPaintableImageSize` drops the image outright above `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE = 20000` (numeric-attrs.ts:104-110). So an imported docx renders one way in the importing session and another (font clamped, image gone) for peers/after reload. The band's own doc claims these ranges are "the range the editor's own controls can reach", which does not cover the import producers.
searchedFor: grep MAX_IMAGE_SIZE / resize clamps in packages/docs/src

samples.summary: `paginatableRowHeight` breaks the previously-held equality between a table `PageLine`'s height and `LayoutTable.rowHeights[row]`, which the out-of-diff renderers, hit-tests and selection geometry still assume
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:132-133` now paginates a row at `paginatableRowHeight(tl.rowHeights[ri], contentHeight)` (0 for non-finite, clamped to `contentHeight * 200`) while `rowLine` is the only thing carrying that height. Every other consumer keeps reading the raw `LayoutTable.rowHeights`: `packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:171` and `:201` (`visibleHeight += rowHeights[rr]`, `cellHeight += rowHeights[r+s]`), `packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:641` (`pl.rowSplitHeight ?? tl.rowHeights[pl.lineIndex]`), `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5518-5522` (row hit-test), `packages/docs/src/view/table-geometry.ts:169`. For a content-derived row height that is NaN or beyond the 200-page bound (reachable via the paste/import producers above, which the new bands do not cover) pagination places/advances by 0 or the clamp while painting and hit-testing use the raw value — overlapping rows and a caret that lands in the wrong row rather than a hang. Fix belongs either on the new helper (write the bounded height back into `tl.rowHeights`) or on those readers.

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (plural) is a newly added exported function with no callers and is not re-exported from either package entry
samples.evidence: Defined at `packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts:42`; a repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeights` returns only that definition (plus prior review artefacts under `.agent-review/`). `packages/docs/src/index.ts:95` and `packages/docs/src/node.ts:135` export only `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` / `normalizeRowHeight`, so it is neither used internally nor part of the public surface — knip's unused-export lane covers this.
searchedFor: read index.ts / node.ts export lists in the diff

samples.summary: The list-level ceiling now has a single home (`MAX_LIST_LEVEL`) that the slides PPTX exporter still hardcodes, so the two will drift
samples.evidence: The diff centralises the ceiling and makes `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:351` import it, but `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:85` still returns `` ` lvl="${Math.min(8, n)}"` `` with a literal 8. Slides already depends on `@wafflebase/docs` (it imports from it throughout, e.g. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts` module header) and could name `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`. Still correct today; a change to the constant would silently desync the PPTX export.
